Invariant Gibbs Measures and a.s. Global Well-Posedness for Coupled KdV Systems

Tadahiro Oh Address: Tadahiro Oh
Department of Mathematics
University of Toronto
40 St. George St, Rm 6290, Toronto, ON M5S 2E4, Canada Email address: oh@math.toronto.edu
Abstract.

We continue our study of the well-posedness theory of a one-parameter family of coupled KdV-type systems in the periodic setting. When the value of a coupling parameter α∈(0,4)∖{1}\alpha\in(0,4)\setminus\{1\}, we show that the Gibbs measure is invariant under the flow and the system is globally well-posed almost surely on the statistical ensemble, provided that certain Diophantine conditions are satisfied.

Key words and phrases: 
KdV; well-posedness; Gibbs measure; Diophantine Conditions
2000 Mathematics Subject Classification
35Q53

1. Introduction

In this paper, we consider coupled KdV systems of the form:

(1) {ut+a11​ux​x​x+a12​vx​x​x+b1​u​ux+b2​u​vx+b3​ux​v+b4​v​vx=0vt+a21​ux​x​x+a22​vx​x​x+b5​u​ux+b6​u​vx+b7​ux​v+b8​v​vx=0(u,v)|t=0=(u0,v0)\begin{cases}u_{t}+a_{11}u_{xxx}+a_{12}v_{xxx}+b_{1}uu_{x}+b_{2}uv_{x}+b_{3}u_{x}v+b_{4}vv_{x}=0\\ v_{t}+a_{21}u_{xxx}+a_{22}v_{xxx}+b_{5}uu_{x}+b_{6}uv_{x}+b_{7}u_{x}v+b_{8}vv_{x}=0\\ (u,v)\big|_{t=0}=(u_{0},v_{0})\end{cases}

in the periodic setting, where A=(a11a12a21a22)A=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}a_{11}&a_{12}\\ a_{21}&a_{22}\end{smallmatrix}\bigr) is self-adjoint, and uu and vv are real-valued functions. There are several systems of this type: the Gear-Grimshaw system [9], the Hirota-Satsuma system [12], the Majda-Biello system [16], etc. By applying the space-time scale changes along with the diagonalization of AA, one can reduce (1) to

(2) {ut+ux​x​x+b1~​u​ux+b2~​u​vx+b3~​ux​v+b4~​v​vx=0vt+α​vx​x​x+b5~​u​ux+b6~​u​vx+b7~​ux​v+b8~​v​vx=0(u,v)|t=0=(u0,v0),\begin{cases}u_{t}+u_{xxx}+\widetilde{b_{1}}uu_{x}+\widetilde{b_{2}}uv_{x}+\widetilde{b_{3}}u_{x}v+\widetilde{b_{4}}vv_{x}=0\\ v_{t}+\alpha v_{xxx}+\widetilde{b_{5}}uu_{x}+\widetilde{b_{6}}uv_{x}+\widetilde{b_{7}}u_{x}v+\widetilde{b_{8}}vv_{x}=0\\ (u,v)\big|_{t=0}=(u_{0},v_{0}),\end{cases}

where α≠0\alpha\neq 0, (x,t)∈𝕋×ℝ(x,t)\in\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R} with 𝕋=[0,2​π)\mathbb{T}=[0,2\pi).

In this paper, we assume that (2) has a Hamiltonian HH of the form “H⁡(u,v)=12​∫ux2+α​vx2+H(u,v)=\frac{1}{2}\int u_{x}^{2}+\alpha v_{x}^{2}+nonlinear terms” and that both HH and N⁡(u,v)=12​∫u2+b​v2N(u,v)=\frac{1}{2}\int u^{2}+bv^{2}, for some b>0b>0, are conserved under the flow of (2). (Note that this is the case for the Gear-Grimshaw and the Majda-Biello systems among other coupled KdV systems.) When α≠1\alpha\neq 1, it is shown in [18] that there is an interval I0I_{0} around α=1\alpha=1 such that particular resonances occur for α∈I0∖{1}\alpha\in I_{0}\setminus\{1\} which are not present when α=1\alpha=1. We show that, for α∈I0∖{1}\alpha\in I_{0}\setminus\{1\}, the Gibbs measure d​μ=Z−1​exp⁡(−β​H​(u,v))​∏x∈𝕋d​u​(x)⊗d​v​(x)d\mu=Z^{-1}\exp(-\beta H(u,v))\prod_{x\in\mathbb{T}}du(x)\otimes dv(x) is invariant under the flow (2) and that (2) is globally well-posed almost surely on the statistical ensemble, provided that certain Diophantine conditions are satisfied.

As a model example, we consider the Majda-Biello system:

(3) {ut+ux​x​x+v​vx=0vt+α​vx​x​x+(u​v)x=0(u,v)|t=0=(u0,v0),⁡(x,t)∈𝕋×ℝ,\begin{cases}u_{t}+u_{xxx}+vv_{x}=0\\ v_{t}+\alpha v_{xxx}+(uv)_{x}=0\\ (u,v)\big|_{t=0}=(u_{0},v_{0}),\end{cases}\ (x,t)\in\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R},

where 𝕋=[0,2​π)\mathbb{T}=[0,2\pi), 0<α≤40<\alpha\leq 4, and uu and vv are real-valued functions. This system has been proposed by Majda and Biello [16] as a reduced asymptotic model to study the nonlinear resonant interactions of long wavelength equatorial Rossby waves and barotropic Rossby waves with a significant mid-latitude projection, in the presence of suitable horizontally and vertically sheared zonal mean flows. In [16], the values of α\alpha are numerically determined and they are 0.8990.899, 0.9600.960, and 0.9800.980 for different equatorial Rossby waves. Of particular interest to us is the periodic case because of its challenging mathematical nature as well as its physical relevance of the proposed model (the spatial period for the system before scaling is set as 40,00040,000 km in [16].)

Several conservation laws are known for the system:

(4) E1=∫u​𝑑x,E2=∫v​𝑑x,N⁡(u,v)=12​∫u2+v2​𝑑x,H⁡(u,v)=12​∫ux2+α​vx2−u​v2​𝑑x,E_{1}=\int u\,dx,\ E_{2}=\int v\,dx,\ N(u,v)=\frac{1}{2}\int u^{2}+v^{2}dx,\ H(u,v)=\frac{1}{2}\int u_{x}^{2}+\alpha v_{x}^{2}-uv^{2}dx,

where H⁡(u,v)H(u,v) is the Hamiltonian of the system. There seems to be no other conservation law, suggesting that the Majda-Biello system may not be completely integrable. The system has scaling which is similar to that of KdV and the critical Sobolev index scs_{c} is −32-\frac{3}{2} just like KdV.

First, we review the local and global well-posedness (LWP and GWP) results of (3) from [18], [19]. Note that all the results, except for the global well-posedness on 𝕋\mathbb{T} for α∈(0,1)∪(1,4)\alpha\in(0,1)\cup(1,4), are sharp in the sense that the smoothness/uniform continuity of the solution map fails below the specified regularities. When α=1\alpha=1, we showed in [19] that (3) is globally well-posed in H−12​(𝕋)×H−12​(𝕋)H^{-\frac{1}{2}}(\mathbb{T})\times H^{-\frac{1}{2}}(\mathbb{T}) without the mean 0 condition on the initial data, via the II-method developed by Colliander-Keel-Staffilani-Takaoka-Tao [7] in the vector-valued variants Xp,qs,bX^{s,b}_{p,q} of the Bourgain space Xs,bX^{s,b} [2].

This shows that the GWP obtained via H(2)H^{(2)} is the best possible result using the II-method. Note that there is a gap between s∗​(α)s^{*}(\alpha) and s∗⁣∗​(α)s^{**}(\alpha), unless s∗=1s^{*}=1. In particular, s∗=12+>s∗⁣∗=57+s^{*}=\frac{1}{2}+>s^{**}=\frac{5}{7}+ for a.e. α∈(0,4]∖{1}\alpha\in(0,4]\setminus\{1\}.

In an attempt to fill the gap between the LWP and the GWP results, we consider the Gibbs measure of the form “d​μ=Z−1​exp⁡(−β​H​(u,v))​∏x∈𝕋d​u​(x)⊗d​v​(x)d\mu=Z^{-1}\exp(-\beta H(u,v))\prod_{x\in\mathbb{T}}du(x)\otimes dv(x)”. First recall the following; Given a Hamiltonian flow

{p˙i=∂H∂qiq˙i=−∂H∂pi\begin{cases}\dot{p}_{i}=\frac{\partial H}{\partial q_{i}}\\ \dot{q}_{i}=-\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_{i}}\end{cases}

on ℝ2​n\mathbb{R}^{2n} with Hamiltonian H=H⁡(p1,⋯,pn,q1,⋯,qn)H=H(p_{1},\cdots,p_{n},q_{1},\cdots,q_{n}), Liouville’s theorem states that the Lebesgue measure on ℝ2​n\mathbb{R}^{2n} is invariant under the flow. From the conservation of the Hamiltonian HH, the Gibbs measures e−β​H​∏i=1nd​pi​d​qie^{-\beta H}\prod_{i=1}^{n}dp_{i}dq_{i} are also invariant, where β\beta is the reciprocal temperature. In our context, the Hamiltonian H⁡(u,v)H(u,v) is conserved under the flow of (3). Then, we’d like to use the invariance of the Gibbs measure μ\mu (which holds true in finite dimensional case) to prove a GWP result. At this point, everything is merely formal, which needs to be made rigorous.

In the context of NLS, Lebowitz-Rose-Speer [15] considered the Gibbs measure of the form d​μ=exp⁡(−β​H​(u))​∏x∈𝕋d​u​(x)d\mu=\exp(-\beta H(u))\prod_{x\in\mathbb{T}}du(x) where H⁡(u)H(u) is the Hamiltonian given by H⁡(u)=12​∫|ux|2±1p​∫|u|p​𝑑xH(u)=\frac{1}{2}\int|u_{x}|^{2}\pm\frac{1}{p}\int|u|^{p}dx. In the focusing case (with −-), H⁡(u)H(u) is not bounded from below and this causes a problem. Using the conservation of the L2L^{2} norm, they instead considered the Gibbs measure of the form dμ=exp(−βH(u))χ{∥u∥L2≤B}∏x∈𝕋du(x)d\mu=\exp(-\beta H(u))\chi_{\{\|u\|_{L^{2}}\leq B\}}\prod_{x\in\mathbb{T}}du(x), i.e. with an L2L^{2}-cutoff. This turned out to be a well-defined measure on H12−​(𝕋)=⋂s<12Hs​(𝕋)H^{\frac{1}{2}-}(\mathbb{T})=\bigcap_{s<\frac{1}{2}}H^{s}(\mathbb{T}) (for p<6p<6 with any B>0B>0, and p=6p=6 with sufficiently small BB.) Bourgain [4] continued this study and proved the invariance of μ\mu under the flow of NLS and the global well-posedness almost surely on the statistical ensemble. Note that [4] appeared before the so-called Bourgain’s method [3] or the II-method [7], i.e. there was virtually no method available to establish any GWP result from a LWP result whose regularity was between two conservation laws. This was the case for NLS for 4<p≤64<p\leq 6. We use this idea to obtain a.s. GWP of the Majda-Biello system (3). Recently, Burq-Tzvetkov [6] independently and simultaneously used similar ideas to prove a.s. GWP for the nonlinear wave equation on the unit ball in ℝ3\mathbb{R}^{3} under the radial symmetry. Also, see other work by Tzvetkov related to this subject [21], [22].

For the Majda-Biello system (3), we have H⁡(u,v)=12​∫ux2+α​vx2−u​v2​𝑑xH(u,v)=\frac{1}{2}\int u_{x}^{2}+\alpha v_{x}^{2}-uv^{2}dx. It is known (c.f. Zhidokov [23]) that the Wiener measure dρ=Z~−1exp(−12∫ux2+αvx2dx)∏x∈𝕋du(x)⊗dv(x)d\rho=\widetilde{Z}^{-1}\exp(-\frac{1}{2}\int u_{x}^{2}+\alpha v_{x}^{2}dx)\prod_{x\in\mathbb{T}}du(x)\otimes dv(x) is a well-defined countably additive measure on H12−​(𝕋)×H12−​(𝕋)H^{\frac{1}{2}-}(\mathbb{T})\times H^{\frac{1}{2}-}(\mathbb{T}). Since −12∫uv2dx-\frac{1}{2}\int uv^{2}dx is not sign-definite, we need to add an L2L^{2} cutoff in considering the Gibbs measure (weighted Wiener measure) as in [15] and [4]. Then, dμ=Z−1exp(12∫uv2dx)χ{∥(u,v)∥L2≤B}dρd\mu=Z^{-1}\exp(\frac{1}{2}\int uv^{2}dx)\chi_{\{\|(u,v)\|_{L^{2}}\leq B\}}d\rho is a well-defined countably additive measure on H12−​(𝕋)×H12−​(𝕋)H^{\frac{1}{2}-}(\mathbb{T})\times H^{\frac{1}{2}-}(\mathbb{T}). When α=1\alpha=1, the invariance of the Gibbs measure μ\mu directly follows from Bourgain’s argument for KdV in [4] and the GWP of (3) in H−12​(𝕋)×H−12​(𝕋)H^{-\frac{1}{2}}(\mathbb{T})\times H^{-\frac{1}{2}}(\mathbb{T}) obtained in [19].

Now, recall that for α∈(0,4)∖{1}\alpha\in(0,4)\setminus\{1\}, the Majda-Biello system (3) is LWP in Hs​(𝕋)×Hs​(𝕋)H^{s}(\mathbb{T})\times H^{s}(\mathbb{T}) only for s>12+12​max⁡(νc1,νd1,νd2)≥12s>\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\max(\nu_{c_{1}},\nu_{d_{1}},\nu_{d_{2}})\geq\frac{1}{2} and is C3C^{3} ill-posed for s<12+12​max⁡(νc1,νd1,νd2)s<\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\max(\nu_{c_{1}},\nu_{d_{1}},\nu_{d_{2}}) in the sense that the solution map is not C3C^{3} (c.f. [18].) i.e. the flow of (3) is not well-defined on the support of the Gibbs measure μ\mu in terms of the usual Sobolev spaces. We instead consider the Cauchy problem for (u0,v0)∈Hs1,s2​(𝕋)×Hs1,s2​(𝕋)(u_{0},v_{0})\in H^{s_{1},s_{2}}(\mathbb{T})\times H^{s_{1},s_{2}}(\mathbb{T}), where

(18) ‖ϕ‖Hs1,s2=‖ϕ‖Hs1+supn⟨n⟩s2​|ϕ^​(n)|<∞\|\phi\|_{H^{s_{1},s_{2}}}=\|\phi\|_{H^{s_{1}}}+\sup_{n}\langle n\rangle^{s_{2}}|\widehat{\phi}(n)|<\infty

for some s1,s2s_{1},s_{2} with 0<s1<12<s2<10<s_{1}<\frac{1}{2}<s_{2}<1 (to be determined later.) First, recall that, as mentioned in Remark 1.2, the bilinear estimates (7) and (8) fail for s≤12s\leq\frac{1}{2} only at 4 frequencies near the resonances. supn⟨n⟩s2​|ϕ^​(n)|\sup_{n}\langle n\rangle^{s_{2}}|\widehat{\phi}(n)| in (18) exactly controls these particular resonances with the higher regularity s2>12+12​max⁡(νc1,νd1,νd2)s_{2}>\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\max(\nu_{c_{1}},\nu_{d_{1}},\nu_{d_{2}}). We have the following theorem.

Theorem 1.

Let α∈(0,4)∖{1}\alpha\in(0,4)\setminus\{1\} and max⁡(νc1,νd1,νd2)<1\max(\nu_{c_{1}},\nu_{d_{1}},\nu_{d_{2}})<1. Assume the mean 0 condition on u0u_{0}. Let 14<s1<12<s2<1\frac{1}{4}<s_{1}<\frac{1}{2}<s_{2}<1 with 2​s1>s2>12+12​max⁡(νc1,νd1,νd2)2s_{1}>s_{2}>\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\max(\nu_{c_{1}},\nu_{d_{1}},\nu_{d_{2}}). Then, the Majda-Biello system (3) is locally well-posed in Hs1,s2​(𝕋)×Hs1,s2​(𝕋)H^{s_{1},s_{2}}(\mathbb{T})\times H^{s_{1},s_{2}}(\mathbb{T}).

As seen in Bourgain’s work on mKdV and Zakharov system [4], [5], we have μ⁡(Hs1,s2×Hs1,s2)=1\mu(H^{s_{1},s_{2}}\times H^{s_{1},s_{2}})=1 for 0<s1<12<s2<10<s_{1}<\frac{1}{2}<s_{2}<1. i.e. Hs1,s2​(𝕋)×Hs1,s2​(𝕋)H^{s_{1},s_{2}}(\mathbb{T})\times H^{s_{1},s_{2}}(\mathbb{T}) contains the full support of μ\mu. In [4], Bourgain proved the invariance of the Gibbs measure and a.s. GWP of mKdV by establishing an improved local well-posedness in Hs1,s2H^{s_{1},s_{2}} with s1=12−s_{1}=\frac{1}{2}- and s2=1−s_{2}=1-. Following his argument, we obtain the a.s. global well-posedness of (3), using the finite dimensional approximation to (3) along with the invariance of the finite dimensional Gibbs measure.

Theorem 2.

Let α∈(0,4)∖{1}\alpha\in(0,4)\setminus\{1\} and max⁡(νc1,νd1,νd2)<1\max(\nu_{c_{1}},\nu_{d_{1}},\nu_{d_{2}})<1. Assume the mean 0 condition on u0u_{0}. Then, the Gibbs measure μ\mu (with an L2L^{2}-cutoff) is invariant under the flow of (3), and (3) is globally well-posed a.s. on the statistical ensemble.

We point out that Theorem 2 does not fill the gap between the LWP and GWP of (3) as we initially hoped. However, it does establish a new GWP result for almost every α∈(0,4)∖{1}\alpha\in(0,4)\setminus\{1\} which can not be obtained by the methods in [18] and [19].

This work is a part of the author’s Ph.D. thesis [17]. This paper is organized as follows: In Section 2, we introduce some standard notations. In Section 3, we go over the basic theory of Gaussian Hilbert spaces and abstract Wiener spaces, and we give the precise meaning to the Gibbs measure μ\mu. In Section 4, we introduce the function spaces and linear estimates. Then, we prove Theorem 1 in Section 5, and extend this local result to a.s. GWP in Section 6. We also establish the invariance of the Gibbs measure μ\mu. In Appendix, we present the proof of a probabilistic lemma from Section 3.

3. Gaussian Measure in Hilbert Space and Abstract Wiener Space

In this section, we go over the basic theory of Gaussian measures in Hilbert spaces and abstract Wiener spaces and provide the precise meaning of the Gibbs measure “d​μ=Z−1​exp⁡(−β​H​(u,v))​∏x∈𝕋d​u​(x)⊗d​v​(x)d\mu=Z^{-1}\exp(-\beta H(u,v))\prod_{x\in\mathbb{T}}du(x)\otimes dv(x)” appearing in Section 1. For simplicity, we set the reciprocal temperature β=1\beta=1. For details, see Zhidokov [23], Gross [11], and Kuo [14].

First, recall (centered) Gaussian measures in ℝn\mathbb{R}^{n}. Let n∈ℕn\in\mathbb{N} and BB be a symmetric positive n×nn\times n matrix with real entries. The Borel measure ρ\rho in ℝn\mathbb{R}^{n} with the density

d​ρ​(x)=1(2​π)n​det(B)​exp⁡(−12​⟨B−1​x,x⟩ℝn)d\rho(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{(2\pi)^{n}\det(B)}}\exp\big(-\tfrac{1}{2}\langle B^{-1}x,x\rangle_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}\big)

is called a (nondegenerate centered ) Gaussian measure in ℝn\mathbb{R}^{n}. Note that ρ⁡(ℝn)=1\rho(\mathbb{R}^{n})=1.

Now, we consider the analogous definition for the infinite dimensional (centered) Gaussian measures. Let HH be a real separable Hilbert space and B:H→HB:H\to H be a linear positive self-adjoint operator (generally not bounded) with eigenvalues {λn}n∈ℕ\{\lambda_{n}\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}} and the corresponding eigenvectors {en}n∈ℕ\{e_{n}\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}} forming an orthonormal basis of HH. We call a set M⊂HM\subset H cylindrical if there exists an integer n≥1n\geq 1 and a Borel set F⊂ℝnF\subset\mathbb{R}^{n} such that

(19) M={x∈H:(⟨x,e1⟩H,⋯,⟨x,en⟩H)∈F}.M=\big\{x\in H:(\langle x,e_{1}\rangle_{H},\cdots,\langle x,e_{n}\rangle_{H})\in F\big\}.

For a fixed operator BB as above, we denote by 𝒜\mathcal{A} the set of all cylindrical subsets of HH. Note that 𝒜\mathcal{A} is a field. Then, the centered Gaussian measure in HH with the correlation operator BB is defined as the additive (but not countably additive in general) measure ρ\rho defined on the field 𝒜\mathcal{A} via

(20) ρ(M)=(2π)−n2∏j=1nλj−12∫Fe−12∑j=1nλj−1xj2dx1⋯dxn, for M∈𝒜 as in (19). \rho(M)=(2\pi)^{-\frac{n}{2}}\prod_{j=1}^{n}\lambda_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\int_{F}e^{-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\lambda_{j}^{-1}x_{j}^{2}}dx_{1}\cdots dx_{n},\text{ for }M\in\mathcal{A}\text{ as in \eqref{CYLINDER}. }

The following theorem tells us when this Gaussian measure ρ\rho is countably additive.

Theorem 3.1.

The Gaussian measure ρ\rho defined in (20) is countably additive on the field 𝒜\mathcal{A} if and only if BB is an operator of trace class, i.e. ∑n=1∞λn<∞\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\lambda_{n}<\infty. If the latter holds, then the minimal σ\sigma-field ℳ\mathcal{M} containing the field 𝒜\mathcal{A} of all cylindrical sets is the Borel σ\sigma-field on HH.

Consider a sequence of the finite dimensional Gaussian measures {ρn}n∈ℕ\{\rho_{n}\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}} as follows. For fixed n∈ℕn\in\mathbb{N}, let ℳn\mathcal{M}_{n} be the set of all cylindrical sets in HH of the form (19) with this fixed nn and arbitrary Borel sets F⊂ℝnF\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}. ρn(M)=(2π)−n2∏j=1nλj−12∫Fe−12∑j=1nλj−1xj2dx1⋯dxn\rho_{n}(M)=(2\pi)^{-\frac{n}{2}}\prod_{j=1}^{n}\lambda_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\int_{F}e^{-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\lambda_{j}^{-1}x_{j}^{2}}dx_{1}\cdots dx_{n}

for M∈ℳnM\in\mathcal{M}_{n}, we obtain a countably additive measure ρn\rho_{n} defined on ℳn\mathcal{M}_{n}. Then, we have

Let ρ\rho in (20) be countably additive. Then, {ρn}n∈ℕ\{\rho_{n}\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}} constructed above converges weakly to ρ\rho as n→∞n\to\infty.

Unfortunately, it is shown in [18] that (3) is ill-posed in Hs×HsH^{s}\times H^{s} for s<12s<\frac{1}{2} when α∈(0,4)∖{1}\alpha\in(0,4)\setminus\{1\}. Recall the following definitions [14]: Given a real separable Hilbert space HH with norm ∥⋅∥\|\cdot\|, let ℱ\mathcal{F} denote the set of finite dimensional orthogonal projections ℙ\mathbb{P} of HH. Then, define a cylinder set EE by E={x∈H:ℙ​x∈F}E=\{x\in H:\mathbb{P}x\in F\} where ℙ∈ℱ\mathbb{P}\in\mathcal{F} and FF is a Borel subset of ℙ​H\mathbb{P}H, and let ℛ\mathcal{R} denote the collection of such cylinder sets. Note that ℛ\mathcal{R} is a field but not a σ\sigma-field. Then, the Gauss measure ρ\rho on HH is defined by

ρ⁡(E)=(2​π)−n2​∫Fe−‖x‖22​𝑑x\rho(E)=(2\pi)^{-\frac{n}{2}}\int_{F}e^{-\frac{\|x\|^{2}}{2}}dx

for E∈ℛE\in\mathcal{R}, where n=dim​ℙ​Hn=\text{dim}\mathbb{P}H and d​xdx is the Lebesgue measure on ℙ​H\mathbb{P}H. It is known that ρ\rho is finitely additive but not countably additive in ℛ\mathcal{R}.

A seminorm |||⋅||||||\cdot||| in HH is called measurable if for every ε>0\varepsilon>0, there exists ℙ0∈ℱ\mathbb{P}_{0}\in\mathcal{F} such that ρ⁡(‖|ℙ​x|‖>ε)<ε\rho(|||\mathbb{P}x|||>\varepsilon)<\varepsilon for ℙ∈ℱ\mathbb{P}\in\mathcal{F} orthogonal to ℙ0\mathbb{P}_{0}. Any measurable seminorm is weaker than the norm of HH, and HH is not complete with respect to |||⋅||||||\cdot||| unless HH is finite dimensional. Let BB be the completion of HH with respect to |||⋅||||||\cdot||| and denote by ii the inclusion map of HH into BB. The triple (i,H,B)(i,H,B) is called an abstract Wiener space.

(34) ‖η2​T∂x(uv)‖Zαs1,s2\displaystyle\left\|\eta_{{}_{2T}}\partial_{x}(uv)\right\|_{Z_{\alpha}^{s_{1},s_{2}}} ≲Tθ​‖u‖Ys1,s2​‖v‖Yαs1,s2,\displaystyle\lesssim T^{\theta}\|u\|_{Y^{s_{1},s_{2}}}\|v\|_{Y_{\alpha}^{s_{1},s_{2}}},

for some θ>0\theta>0. For the rest of this section, we first present the proof of (31) and (32) in Propositions 5.2, 5.3, and 5.4. Then, we mention how to obtain the positive power of TT as in (33) and (34).

6. Global Well-Posedness on the Statistical Ensemble and the
Invariance of the Gibbs Measure

Once we establish the local well-posedness of (3) via the fixed point theorem and tightness of μN\mu_{N} and μ\mu (Lemma 3.5), Bourgain’s argument in [4] yields the global well-posedness a.s. on the statistical ensemble. As for the invariance of the Gibbs measure μ\mu (Theorem 6.6), we follow the argument in Rey-Bellet and Thomas [20]. We include these arguments for the sake of completeness.

Consider the finite dimensional approximation to (3):

(50) {utN+ux​x​xN+ℙN​(vN​vxN)=0vtN+α​vx​x​xN+ℙN​((uN​vN)x)=0,\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}u^{N}_{t}+u^{N}_{xxx}+\mathbb{P}_{N}(v^{N}v^{N}_{x})=0\\ v^{N}_{t}+\alpha v^{N}_{xxx}+\mathbb{P}_{N}\big((u^{N}v^{N})_{x}\big)=0,\end{array}\right.

with (uN​(x,0),vN​(x,0))=(u0N​(x),v0N​(x))=(ℙN​u0​(x),ℙN​v0​(x))\big(u^{N}(x,0),v^{N}(x,0)\big)=\big(u_{0}^{N}(x),v_{0}^{N}(x)\big)=\big(\mathbb{P}_{N}u_{0}(x),\mathbb{P}_{N}v_{0}(x)\big) for N→∞N\to\infty. In the following, we assume that the mean of u0u_{0} is 0. Note that ∫(uN)2+(vN)2​𝑑x\int(u^{N})^{2}+(v^{N})^{2}dx is conserved under the finite dimensional flow. Moreover, the finite dimensional truncation of the Hamiltonian

(51) HN​(u,v)=12​∫(uxN)2+α​(vxN)2−ℙN​(uN​(vN)2)​𝑑xH_{N}(u,v)=\frac{1}{2}\int(u^{N}_{x})^{2}+\alpha(v^{N}_{x})^{2}-\mathbb{P}_{N}\big(u^{N}(v^{N})^{2}\big)dx

is conserved as well. Therefore, by Liouville’s Theorem, μN\mu_{N} is invariant under the flow of (50).

In the following, we first establish the a.s. GWP of (50) (with an explicit growth bound modulo small set), independent of NN. Then, using this and the invariance of μN\mu_{N}, we show the a.s. GWP of (3) and the invariance of μ\mu.
